note: DRAFT positional playbook for Shareholders' Agreements governed by Indian law. Covers tag-along/drag-along thresholds, lock-in, board composition, reserved matters, non-compete, liquidated damages, and exit. No in-house lawyer has approved these positions.
applies_to: Shareholders' agreements for Indian private limited companies
not_legal_advice: Every finding is a POTENTIAL_ISSUE against a company standard, not a statement of law.

rules.why: Lock-in restricts exit. 1 year is standard for financial investors; 2 years is acceptable for strategic; above 3 years is unusual for a minority stake and flags NEEDS_LAWYER.

Tag-along protects minority shareholders from being stranded. A threshold above 50% renders it useless since most exits are structured below that. Uses max_amount since the value is a percentage number.

starting.text: 75% of total shareholding required to drag

rules.why: Drag-along forces minority to sell. Higher threshold = better minority protection. Below 51% means a bare majority can force everyone out.

Post-term non-competes in SHAs are contentious under Indian Contract Act s.27. The starting position is no non-compete. If unavoidable, it must be narrow in scope and duration. Above 3 years is almost certainly unenforceable and flags NEEDS_LAWYER.
Board composition for a minority investor. 1 seat is standard for a 10-25% stake. More than 2 seats for a minority investor shifts control disproportionately.

Liquidated damages in SHAs are rarely enforced by Indian courts if they amount to a penalty (Indian Contract Act s.74). The starting position is no LD clause. If present, it must be proportionate to actual loss.
SHA for an Indian company should be governed by Indian law. Foreign governing law makes enforcement of reserved matters and board rights difficult.
Arbitration seat determines procedural law. Indian seat preferred; Singapore acceptable for cross-border deals as Indian courts enforce Singapore awards under the NY Convention.
Exit timeline sets expectation for liquidity event. 5 years is standard PE; 7 years for growth equity. Above 10 years locks capital with no realistic exit path.
Information rights frequency. Monthly is investor-friendly; quarterly is company-friendly. No dealbreaker since any reasonable frequency is acceptable.
